items.originalTitle: 梅赛德斯一度以为拿下杆位，直到诺里斯出现
items.summaryEn: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff briefly believed Kimi Antonelli had secured pole position for the Spanish Grand Prix, but Lando Norris snatched it away by the slightest margin.
detailZh: 梅赛德斯一度以为拿下杆位，直到兰多·诺里斯出现
基米·安东内利在终点线前被诺里斯以最微弱的优势击败，无缘马德里赛道杆位
梅赛德斯F1车队领队托托·沃尔夫一度认为基米·安东内利已为西班牙大奖赛夺得杆位——直到兰多·诺里斯将其夺走。
安东内利在新马德里赛道的Q3第二轮中，较其首轮1分32.140秒的成绩明显提升，跑出1分31.835秒，比所有对手至少快0.178秒。
除了一个人。诺里斯首轮成绩为1分32.525秒，尽管据迈凯伦领队安德烈亚·斯特拉描述，他在最后一弯损失了0.3秒，但他仍以1分31.824秒跃升至杆位。
沃尔夫显然没有预料到这一点——但当被问及这是丢失的杆位还是获得第二名时，他更愿意看到积极的一面。
“从那个角度看，是获得的，”沃尔夫告诉奥地利广播公司ORF。“在这个周末之前，我从不相信我们能在这种赛道布局下处于领先。”
“当刘易斯冲过终点线时，似乎很清楚我们要赢了。然后兰多在这样的条件下——天气突然变得如此炎热，而他非常擅长管理后轮过热——跑出了那样一圈。完美无瑕。”
迈凯伦在Q3之前的所有练习赛和排位赛阶段都比梅赛德斯慢，因此沃尔夫没有预料到这种性能转变。
“这也让我们感到惊讶，”他说。“但兰多过去曾展示过，他偶尔能跑出那样一圈。尤其是在尽可能控制后轴过热方面。在这方面，我认为他独一档。”
当被问及他预计比赛将如何展开时，沃尔夫特别指出了冠军争夺。刘易斯·汉密尔顿是梅赛德斯在车手冠军争夺中的主要挑战者，目前落后安东内利76分，而乔治·拉塞尔仅领先其前队友10分。
“最重要的是我们不要撞到任何东西；那对成本上限不利，”他指出。“不要输给刘易斯和法拉利积分。我认为在这里你必须得分，顺利完赛，希望能登上领奖台，希望能领先刘易斯。这样我们就达到了目标。”
detailEn: Mercedes thought it had pole position until Lando Norris came along
Kimi Antonelli was beaten by Norris on the line, by the slightest of margins, for Madring pole
Mercedes Formula 1 team principal Toto Wolff briefly believed Kimi Antonelli had taken pole position for the Spanish Grand Prix – until Lando Norris snatched it away.
Antonelli markedly improved on his initial 1m32.140s on his second Q3 run at the new Madring track, setting a 1m31.835s and outpacing all his rivals by at least 0.178s.

All, but one. Norris, whose first effort was a 1m32.525s, vaulted himself to pole position with a 1m31.824s, despite what was described by McLaren team principal Andrea Stella as a three-tenth loss in the final corner.
Wolff definitely didn’t see it coming – but preferred to see the glass half full, when asked if this was a lost pole position or a gained second place.
“It’s gained, looking at it that way,” Wolff told Austrian broadcaster ORF. “Before the weekend, I never believed we’d be at the front on this track layout.

“When Lewis crossed the line, it seemed clear we were winning this. And then Lando puts in a lap like that under conditions that suddenly got so hot, where he is so good at managing rear overheating. It's flawless.”
McLaren had been slower than Mercedes in all practice sessions and qualifying segments prior to Q3, so Wolff didn’t expect this shift in performance.

“That surprised us, too,” he said. “But Lando has shown in the past that he can occasionally pull out a lap like that. Especially when it comes to getting a handle on rear axle overheating as best as possible. And in that regard, I think he's in a league of his own.”

Asked how he expected the race to unfold, Wolff notably pointed to the title battle. Lewis Hamilton, who is Mercedes’ main challenger for the drivers’ title, currently has a 76-point deficit to Antonelli, while George Russell is just 10 points ahead of his former team-mate.

“The most important thing is that we don't crash into anything; that wouldn't be good for the cost cap,” he pointed out. “And not losing points to Lewis and Ferrari. I think here you have to score, drive home, hopefully end up on the podium, hopefully ahead of Lewis. Then we’ve reached our goals.”

诺里斯首轮成绩为1分32.525秒，据迈凯伦领队安德烈亚·斯特拉描述，他在最后一弯损失了0.3秒。
沃尔夫表示，迈凯伦在Q3前所有练习和排位阶段都比梅赛德斯慢，这一性能转变出乎意料。
keyPointsEn: Antonelli set a 1m31.835s in the second Q3 run, at least 0.178s faster than all rivals, but Norris took pole with a 1m31.824s.
Norris's first effort was a 1m32.525s, and according to McLaren team principal Andrea Stella, he lost three-tenths in the final corner.
Wolff said McLaren had been slower than Mercedes in all practice sessions and qualifying segments before Q3, making the performance shift unexpected.

items.titleZh: 维斯塔潘：要赢西班牙大奖赛需先弄清在哪里超车
items.summaryZh: 维斯塔潘在F1西班牙大奖赛排位赛中位列第三，落后杆位得主诺里斯和梅赛德斯车手安东内利仅略超十分之一秒。他表示，鉴于马德里街道赛道超车极为困难，若要击败诺里斯夺冠，自己仍需弄清在哪里超车。

items.originalTitle: 维斯塔潘：要赢西班牙大奖赛需先弄清在哪里超车
items.summaryEn: Max Verstappen qualified third for the F1 Spanish Grand Prix, just over a tenth slower than polesitter Lando Norris and Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli. He said he still needs to figure out where to overtake if he is to beat Norris to victory, given how difficult passing is expected to be at the Madring street circuit.
detailZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘：“我需要弄清在哪里超车”才能赢得F1西班牙大奖赛
维斯塔潘担心马德里街道赛道缺乏超车机会，这将阻碍他周日争夺胜利的可能
马克斯·维斯塔潘表示，如果要在F1西班牙大奖赛中击败兰多·诺里斯夺冠，他仍需弄清在哪里超车。
维斯塔潘在马德里新街道赛道的排位赛中位列第三，仅比杆位得主诺里斯和梅赛德斯的基米·安东内利慢了略超十分之一秒。
当被问及能否挑战迈凯伦争夺胜利时，鉴于马德里街道赛道预计超车极为困难，这位红牛车手表示怀疑。
“这会很艰难，”他说。“我的意思是，就算，比如说，最好的情况，你更快，你也超不过去。没有可以超车的弯角。所以，你得依赖别人轮胎严重退化。”
“长距离跑非常艰难，每个人的轮胎磨损都很大，所以这可能是明天的关键点。但即便如此，我仍然需要找到一个可以超车的弯角。”
维斯塔潘对排位赛表现相当满意。就单圈时间差距而言，这是自摩纳哥站以来他距离杆位最近的一次，当时他仅落后安东内利0.043秒。
“还可以，”他说。“我的意思是，今年我进入前三的次数不多，所以对我来说，我认为我们排位赛跑得不错。”
“赛车，我认为我们做了一些不错的改进，而且我觉得，我们一到这里，就处在一个，可以说，不错的窗口。然后，我认为我们一直有点挣扎的地方始终是最后一个计时段，我们似乎无法像竞争对手那样做好能量部署，这当然让匹配他们变得非常困难。”
“但总的来说，我对一切进展相当满意。每一节排位赛，从Q1到Q2再到Q3，都有不错的提升。没有什么我觉得自己留下的余地，更多是赛车本身我们知道存在的一些局限，加上最后一个计时段的能量部署，我们似乎可能没有完全做好。但这就是排位赛。我的意思是，正赛又是完全不同的。”
鉴于维斯塔潘在Q2以0.160秒的优势领先安东内利，他是否本可以期望更好的结果？
“我想我也是唯一使用了两套轮胎的人之一，所以这其实不是公平的比较，”他细致地指出。
detailEn: Max Verstappen: ‘I need to figure out where to overtake’ to win F1 Spanish GP
Verstappen fears the lack of passing opportunities at Madring will hinder a potential bid for victory on Sunday
Max Verstappen says he still needs to figure out where to overtake if he is to beat Lando Norris to victory in Formula 1’s Spanish Grand Prix.
Verstappen qualified third at Madrid’s new street circuit, just over a tenth slower than polesetter Norris and Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli.
Asked if he could challenge the McLaren for victory, the Red Bull driver was skeptical, given how tricky overtaking is expected to be at Madring.

“It will be tough,” he said. “I mean, even, let’s say, best-case scenario, you are faster, you can’t pass. There are no corners where you can pass. So, you need to rely on people deg-ing very aggressively.
“The long runs were very tough, a lot of [tyre] deg for everyone, so that will be probably the key point tomorrow. But even with that, I need to still figure out a corner where to pass.”

Verstappen was fairly satisfied with his qualifying performance. In terms of lap time deficit, this is the closest he has been to pole position since Monaco, where he was just 0.043s down on Antonelli.
“It was alright," he said. “I mean, I haven’t been here so much this year in the top three, so for me I think we had a good qualifying.

“The car, I think we made some nice improvements, but it was also, I think, straight away when we arrived here in, let’s say, a decent window. And then, I think where we just struggle a little bit is always that final sector, where we just don’t seem to get our deployment like our competitors, and that makes it, of course, very tough to match.

“But, overall, I’m quite happy with how everything went. Every qualifying, from Q1 to Q2 to Q3, just nice progression. There were not really things that, I guess, I left on the table, just more like a few limitations within the car that we know we have, plus the deployment in the final sector where we just didn’t seem to maybe fully get it right. But that’s qualifying. I mean, the race is again very different.”
Could Verstappen actually have hoped for a better result, given he topped Q2 by 0.160s over Antonelli?
“I think I was also one of the only ones that used two sets, so it’s not really a fair comparison,” he nuanced.
keyPointsZh: 维斯塔潘对排位赛表现基本满意，认为这是自摩纳哥站以来他距离杆位最近的一次。
他指出赛车在最后一个计时段表现挣扎，能量部署不如竞争对手。
他提到长距离跑中轮胎磨损严重，这可能是正赛的关键因素。
keyPointsEn: Verstappen was fairly satisfied with his qualifying performance, calling it his closest to pole since Monaco.
He noted the car struggles in the final sector, where its deployment is not as good as competitors'.
He mentioned that tyre degradation was severe on long runs, which could be a key factor in the race.

items.titleZh: 决定马德里首场F1比赛的5大因素
items.summaryZh: F1今日在马德里马德里赛道赛道迎来首场比赛，练习赛、排位赛及F2/F3垫场赛提供了一些线索，但缺乏历史数据意味着比赛仍可能充满意外。
items.originalTitle: 决定马德里首场F1比赛的5大因素
items.summaryEn: Formula 1 heads into the unknown today at the new Madring circuit in Madrid for its first Spanish Grand Prix, with practice, qualifying and support races offering some clues but no racing history meaning surprises are possible.
detailZh: F1各车队和车手在今日的西班牙大奖赛中驶入未知领域，因为这是大奖赛赛车首次在新马德里赛道赛道比赛。这意味着比赛将如何展开存在一些重大疑问，但已有指向潜在答案的线索。
练习赛和排位赛设定了一些预期，F2和F3垫场赛的进行方式也是如此，但这里缺乏可供参考的比赛历史，意味着可能会出现一些意外。
以下是可能影响比赛的五个关键方面。
截至撰写本文时，在马德里赛道举行的五场比赛——两场F2和三场F3——中，第二位发车有四次在起步时取得领先。在周日的F2和F3比赛中，两次都是杆位车手迅速向左移动，以覆盖第二位车手更强的起步。
从电视观众视角看，杆位在左侧，这符合惯例，因为它提供了弯道通常的赛车线，第二位在右侧。
可以肯定，迈凯伦的兰多·诺里斯会非常清楚杆位是否存在任何劣势，这可能意味着他会认识到需要覆盖安东内利。不过，迈凯伦通常良好的起步也可能抵消任何劣势。
发车格不同侧的抓地力往往存在差异，而且每一排也可能不同，但本周末第二位发车位的抓地力比杆位略好一些。这可能意味着安东内利在起步时有机会，而诺里斯需要根据起步情况考虑覆盖他。
马德里赛道的主要超车点是5/5a/6号减速弯，它位于2号弯后长直全油门路段之后，会颠簸路肩。
这在垫场赛中产生了最多的轮对轮较量，但大多数情况导致一辆车、偶尔两辆车切弯。正如乔治·拉塞尔所说，“设计上的一个小遗憾是缺乏清晰的超车机会”，这意味着这个减速弯将是任何人最好的机会。
“总的来说，比赛中超车会非常困难，”红牛的利亚姆·劳森说。
“在那里防守很容易，或者比普通弯道更容易，因为你只需把对方推出减速弯，他就必须归还位置。”
这意味着会有大量无线电抱怨、许多沮丧的进攻，以及在战斗中出错时可能发生碰撞或撞墙。
或者，正如亚历克斯·阿尔本所说，“如果你看了F3和F2比赛，全是车手在减速弯并排，然后抱怨其中一人没有让他们重新超过。”
轮胎退化——包括前轮颗粒化和后轮过热——一直是西班牙大奖赛周末的主要话题之一。
情况已从周五练习赛大幅改善，当时乔治·拉塞尔半开玩笑地说马德里赛道的比赛看起来要进站六次。
事实上，随着赛道橡胶化相当好，现在一停和二停之间在时间上看起来相当微妙。
因此，由于超车似乎很困难，这意味着车队可能倾向于告诉车手管理轮胎，走保守路线以尽量减少进站。
但这对于处理过热轮胎来说都很好；阻止颗粒化则要困难得多。因此，颗粒化的程度可能将是关键。
当被问及比赛会混乱还是平淡时，奥迪的尼科·霍肯伯格说：“看，这真的取决于我们是否出现颗粒化，我认为那将是主要驱动因素。”
“如果我们出现颗粒化，我认为那会相当严重，可能会很混乱。但就像你说的，你知道，你永远不知道。”
颗粒化可能引发转向不足，使高速弯变得非常困难，并引发退化水平迅速上升——带来一些策略复杂性。
所以所有目光都需要关注左前轮胎。
鉴于需要保护轮胎并可能勉强完成一停，安东内利建议“前10圈将是奶奶式驾驶”，而马克斯·维斯塔潘说“你需要依赖别人轮胎退化得非常严重”。
那么，这是否意味着这可能是一场领先者——无论是全场领先还是车群领先——可以大幅减速并轻松挡住一串赛车的比赛？
这是一条防守容易的赛道，用去年的赛车肯定会出现这种情况。
然而，由于能量部署因素，现在有可能利用巨大的动力优势在不太可能的地方完成超车，这意味着如果你过于执着于阻挡对手，你会更加脆弱。
但即使这样做机会也有限，因为有些全油门区域很容易挡住后面的车——昨天卡洛斯·塞恩斯在通往7号弯的上坡路段无意中阻挡瓦尔特利·博塔斯就说明了这一点。
回顾阿塞拜疆大奖赛的历史表明，比赛的特点往往取决于车手的集体心态。
当预测会混乱时——正如巴库多次发生的那样——车手可以改变方法。他们选择稳妥行事，感觉到远离他人的麻烦就能保证积分。
这种策略很好。然而，当每个人都这样做时，结果可能是一种平静，导致比赛沉闷。
凯迪拉克车手瓦尔特利·博塔斯认为，马德里赛道有可能不会带来其布局暗示的不可预测性——就像第一次练习赛零中断那样。
“就像FP1，如果人们太谨慎，那就会发生，”他说。
“但你永远不知道。就是这样的赛道：一个错误就会黄旗、安全车或红旗，所以肯定会有人犯错。”
尽管巴库在混乱与平静之间摇摆的例子，查尔斯·勒克莱尔认为最终马德里会介于两者之间。
“我不会用那些极端，但当然我不知道混乱方面，”他说。
“我认为在这样具有挑战性的赛道上可能会有一些红旗或事故。然而，巴库在超车方面可能相当疯狂，而在这里，我很难看到很多很多超车。”
detailEn: Formula 1’s teams and drivers head into the unknown in today’s Spanish Grand Prix as it’s the first time grand prix cars have raced at the new Madring. And that means there are some big questions about how the race will unfold, but with signposts to the potential answers.

Practice and qualifying have set some expectations, as has the way the Formula 2 and Formula 3 support races have played out, but the lack of racing history here to go on means that there could be some surprises.
Here are five key aspects that could shape the race.

In the five Madring races held at the time of writing - two Formula 2 and three Formula 3 races - second on the grid has taken the lead at the start four times. And in Sunday’s F2 and F3 races, on both occasions the polesitter moved left quickly to cover the stronger start of the driver in second.
Pole position is on the left side as the TV viewer looks at it, which is as per convention as it gives the usual racing line for the corner, with second on the right.

You can be certain that McLaren's Lando Norris will be very well aware if there is any disadvantage to being on pole position, potentially meaning he will recognise the need to cover Antonelli. Then again, it might be that McLaren's generally good launches offset any disadvantage.

There is often a difference in grip on different sides of the grid, as well as the potential for it varying depending on each row, but this weekend the second-placed grid slot has got a little more grip than pole position. That could mean an opportunity for Antonelli at the start, and the need for Norris to consider covering him depending on how the launch goes.
The main passing place at the Madring is the kerb-rattling Turn 5/5a/6 chicane that follows the long flat-out blast from Turn 2.

This has produced the most wheel-to-wheel action in the support races, but with the majority of instances resulting in one, or occasionally both, cars cutting the track. As George Russell put it, "the one small frustration in the design is the lack of clear overtaking opportunities", meaning the chicane is going to be the best chance anyone has.
"It's going to be very hard to overtake in the race in general," said Red Bull's Liam Lawson.
"It's very easy to defend there, or easier than normal corners, because you just push the guy off through the chicane and he has to give the place back."
This means there will be plenty of radio complaining, lots of frustrated attacks and the potential either for a collision or hitting the wall if you get it wrong in battle.
Or, as Alex Albon put it, "if you watched the F3 and F2 races, it was all drivers going side by side in the chicane and then complaining that one of them didn't let them back past."
Tyre degradation – both from front graining and rears overheating – has been one of the big talking points over the Spanish GP weekend.
The situation has improved a lot from Friday practice, when George Russell half-joked that the Madring race looked like it was heading for a six-stopper.
In fact, with the track having rubbered in quite well, things now look quite delicately poised time-wise between a one and a two-stopper.
So, with overtaking appearing to be difficult, that means the likely preference for teams will be to tell drivers to manage tyres and play the conservative route to minimise pit stops.
But that is all well and good for handling overheating tyres; stopping graining is a much harder task. Therefore, the level of graining will potentially be key.
As Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg said about whether the race would be chaotic or processional: “Look, it really depends, if we get graining, if we don't, I think that will be the main driver.
“If we get graining, I think it's going to be quite something and it might be chaotic. But, like you say, you know, you never know.”
Graining could trigger understeer, make the high-speed corners very difficult and trigger a rapid increase in degradation levels – throwing some strategy complications.
So all eyes need to be on those front-left tyres.

Given the need to protect the tyres and potentially eke out a one-stopper, Antonelli suggested "it's going to be grandmother driving in the first 10 laps", while Max Verstappen says "you need to rely on people [tyre] deg-ing very aggressively".
So does that mean this could be one of those races where the leader either of the race overall, or of a pack of cars, can back off dramatically and easily hold up a queue of cars?
It's a track where defending is easy, and with last year's cars it would definitely be on the cards.

However, with the deployment factor, it's now possible to use a huge power advantage to make a drive-by move in an unlikely place, meaning that you are more vulnerable if you are committing to holding up rivals too much.

But, there are limited opportunities even to do that as there are full-throttle zones where it’s easy to keep a car behind - Carlos Sainz inadvertently impeding Valtteri Bottas on the run up the hill to Turn 7 illustrated that yesterday.
A look back through the history of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix has shown that the characteristics of a race can often depend on the collective mindset of the drivers.

When chaos is predicted – as has happened many times in Baku – the drivers can change their approach. They opt to play it safe, sensing that staying out of everyone else’s trouble will guarantee points.
That tactic is all well and good. However, when everyone does it then the result can be a level of calmness that leads to a subdued race.
Cadillac driver Valtteri Bottas thinks it is possible that Madring does not deliver the unpredictability that its layout hints at – as happened when opening practice threw up zero stoppages.
“Like FP1, if people are too cautious, then that can happen,” he said.
“But you just never know. It's a track like that: one mistake and it will be yellow or safety car or red flag, so surely somebody is going to make a mistake.”
Despite the example of Baku bouncing between chaos and calm, Charles Leclerc thinks in the end Madrid will be somewhere in the middle.
“I wouldn't use those extreme ends, but surely I don't know about the chaos in a way,” he said.

“I think there may be some red flags or some incidents on a track that is so challenging like this one. However, Baku can be quite crazy with overtakes, while here, I struggle to see many, many overtakes.”
keyPointsZh: 在马德里赛道已举行的五场F2/F3比赛中，第二位发车四次在起步时取得领先，且本周末第二位发车位的抓地力略优于杆位。
5/5a/6号减速弯是主要超车点，但多数轮对轮较量以切弯告终，乔治·拉塞尔称设计上缺乏清晰超车机会，利亚姆·劳森称防守容易。
轮胎颗粒化和后轮过热是周末焦点，一停与二停策略之间平衡微妙，尼科·霍肯伯格认为颗粒化将是比赛混乱与否的关键。

items.summaryEn: Colton Herta has withdrawn from both races at the Madring Formula 2 round after crashing in Friday qualifying. His car damaged the front, rear and right-hand side when he hit both walls at Turn 19.
detailZh: 科尔顿·赫尔塔退出马德里环赛的两场二级方程式比赛
赫尔塔的周末在马德里排位赛撞车后宣告结束
科尔顿·赫尔塔已退出马德里环赛（马德里赛道）二级方程式分站的两场比赛。
这位Hitech车队的车手在周五于马德里新赛道举行的排位赛中撞车退赛，赛车尾部在19号弯失控甩出。他先后撞上两侧护墙，导致赛车的前部、后部和右侧均受损。
赫尔塔在周六和周日的两场比赛中相继退赛，据报道他感觉“身体不适”。对于他在接下来几轮比赛中是否会出现，没有任何评论。
这位前印地车手决定通过担任凯迪拉克的测试与发展角色来追求自己的F1梦想，但他并没有幻想自己转战F2会是一件容易的事。
然而，他可能没想到会挣扎得如此厉害。赫尔塔在11轮比赛中只有一次排位进入前十，本赛季至今仅获得26分，其中20分来自前五轮。
换句话说，这位加州车手的进步并不明显，而在蒙扎他经历了可以说是本赛季最糟糕的一个周末，两次发生撞车。这已经是他最近六次F2练习和比赛中的第三次事故了。
与此同时，Hitech车队的队友宫田莉桃终于在周六的第76次尝试中赢得了个人首个F2冠军，而同为美国籍的乌戈·乌戈丘乌在周日夺得了2026年F3年度冠军。
法拉利青训车手迪诺·贝戈诺维奇在今天上午晚些时候的F2主赛中，从杆位出发并以统治级的表现赢得了冠军。
红牛青训车手尼古拉·措洛夫仍以177分领跑积分榜，法拉利车手学院车手拉斐尔·卡马拉以170分紧随其后，阿尔派车队的加布里埃莱·米尼以153分、阿莱克斯·邓恩以139分分列其后。
detailEn: Colton Herta withdraws from both Madring F2 races
Herta’s weekend ended after a qualifying crash in Madrid
Colton Herta has withdrawn from both races at the Madring Formula 2 round.

The Hitech driver crashed out of qualifying on Friday at Madrid’s new track, with the rear end slipping away in Turn 19. He hit both walls, damaging the front, the rear and the right-hand side of his car.
Herta successively withdrew from both races on Saturday and Sunday, reportedly feeling “unwell”. No comment was made about his presence or absence at the next rounds.
The former IndyCar runner decided to pursue his F1 dream with a Cadillac test and development role, but was under no illusions that his switch to F2 was going to be easy.

However, he probably didn’t expect to struggle this much. Herta has qualified in the top 10 just once across 11 rounds and has scored 26 points so far this season – 20 of them in the first five rounds.

In other words, the Californian’s progress hasn’t been obvious, and he endured arguably his worst weekend of the season in Monza where he crashed twice. That’s three accidents in his last six F2 sessions.
Meanwhile, Hitech team-mate Ritomo Miyata finally clinched his maiden F2 victory at the 76th time of asking on Saturday, while fellow American Ugo Ugochukwu won the 2026 F3 title on Sunday.
Ferrari protege Dino Beganovic won the F2 feature race later this morning with a commanding drive from pole position.
Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov still leads the championship with 177 points, followed by Ferrari academy driver Rafael Camara (170), and Alpine's Gabriele Mini (153) and Alex Dunne (139).

items.summaryEn: Formula 1 drivers experienced a surprisingly high level of grip on their first visit to the Madrid circuit, while very high tyre degradation has equally surprised teams in the paddock. Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff joked about a six-stop strategy, though the extremely long pitlane in reality appears to favour a one-stopper.
detailZh: 马德里大奖赛会有什么看点？从梅赛德斯的六次进站玩笑，到一条“长达六公里”的维修通道
托托·沃尔夫表示，一练结束后，梅赛德斯的策略部门就在考虑六次进站的比赛。实际上，这条超长的维修通道已经招致批评，而且看起来更有利于一次进站的策略
马德里的这条赛道在首次迎接一级方程式车手时提供了出人意料的高抓地力，这对于一条新赛道来说绝非理所当然。围场里的一些车队对抓地力水平感到意外，不过到目前为止极高的轮胎损耗同样令他们吃惊。
“周末开始的时候挺棘手的，因为这条赛道抓地力非常高，尽管它是一层全新的沥青表面，”梅赛德斯车队领队托托·沃尔夫说。“而且有趣的是，我们遇到的问题和我们预期的完全相反。”
“根据第一个阶段结束后的情况来看，我们的策略总监说：‘六停！’，因为实际上每圈的轮胎衰退达到了十分之八秒。我们从未见过这种情况，但最终，我认为还是会变成一停。”
为什么马德里的轮胎衰退这么严重？
在周五的练习赛之后，轮胎供应商倍耐力也表达了惊讶，倒不是抓地力水平的问题——因为周三赛前测试时抓地力就已经很高了——而是轮胎的衰退程度。
“是的，老实说这确实是个意外，”倍耐力首席工程师西蒙内·贝拉在接受Motorsport.赛车运动网站采访时被问到这个问题时说。“各支车队正在调整赛车的调校，以在性能和长距离轮胎衰退之间找到最佳折中方案。不过，出现这样的数值确实出乎意料。它们超出了我们的预期范围。”
这些数值虽然不像沃尔夫所说的那么极端，但按照一级方程式的标准仍然值得关注——通常这种情况更像是卡塔尔赛道的特征，那里高温与一连串高速弯角相结合。据倍耐力介绍，周五仅因轮胎性能衰减，每圈就损失了约0.2到0.3秒的圈速。
马德里赛道（马德里赛道）迄今为止提供了出乎意料好的抓地力水平，但它对轮胎的损耗非常大
据这家意大利轮胎供应商介绍，马德里出现高磨损的根本原因有两个：轮胎颗粒化（graining）以及后轴常见的热性能衰减。
“在这种光滑的铺装路面和高抓地力水平下，我们会产生轮胎颗粒化现象，”贝拉说。“我们基本上达到了应力的峰值，所以轮胎开始撕裂并扩散颗粒化。”
“这里的颗粒化程度肯定是一个限制因素，车手们能感觉到性能有所下降。这是他们在周五重油量长距离测试中遇到的影响之一，前左轮的颗粒化成为限制因素，导致整个测试过程中弯道中出现转向不足。但我们的后轴也出现了一些热衰减，所以这两种影响的结合造成了相当严重的轮胎退化。”
F1车手批评马德里的维修区通道过长
这显然不会导致六次进站，但据倍耐力表示，这确实让战略权衡变得困难。而车队在阿维德·林德布拉德于第二节自由练习中撞车之后，并没有特别多的长距离测试数据，这让情况更加复杂。
“比赛会发生什么本身就是一个问号。我不想排除任何可能出现的情况，”贝拉说。
在第二次练习赛结束后，倍耐力预测车手们会采用两次进站的策略，但一天之后这一预测被修改为一次进站。原因很简单：马德里的维修通道极长。
诺里斯和维斯塔潘都认为维修通道实在太长了，并指出这是一个设计缺陷。
维修通道实际上被分成了两个部分，因为IFEMA建筑群的一部分位于中间。虽然维修通道确实绕过了1号弯和2号弯，但车手们仍然认为这是马德里赛道（马德里赛道）设计过程中的一个重大失误。
“这条维修通道差不多有六公里长！”兰多·诺里斯在排位赛后的新闻发布会上说。“我们应该把维修通道分成两段：先进站限速区，出了限速区，然后再进一次限速区。这是全年最长的维修通道，也是全年进站损失最大的赛道。这只会让超车变得更难。”
“这会让人们更不愿意进站尝试不同策略。如果我们要新建一条赛道并花费这么多钱，那么这大概是设计赛道时的主要考量之一——设置一条短维修通道，让人们能够顺利进站，从而创造超车机会。”
漫长的维修通道有利于一停策略，尽管按照倍耐力的数据，一停和两停的纯比赛时间是相同的。通常情况下，这本是制造策略多样性的完美场景——这也正是倍耐力想要达到的目标——但马德里的维修通道可能会毁掉这一点。
在比赛前列靠前位置进行提前进站（提前进站）可能引发第二轮进站潮，但这同样是一场赌博，因为在马德里赛道位置至关重要。为了新轮胎放弃赛道位置是有风险的，贝拉也承认这一点。
“另一个因素是，与各车队交流后了解到，在这里超车似乎相当困难，”他说。“如果你处在车流当中，你会损失相当多的性能，而且还会毁掉你的轮胎，因为你失去了气流负载，导致温度升高。所以车流会产生不利影响，并推动大家倾向一停策略。”
除了所有理性因素之外，在马德里不幸随时可能降临，正如贝尔曼在周六所发现的那样。
撇开这些因素不谈，发生撞车——随之而来的安全车或红旗——在马德里也是相当有可能出现的，这意味着运气女神所起的作用可能会比车队任何可以理性评估的因素都要大。
车队需要为各种不同的情景做好准备，这也是为什么一些车队故意在周五和周六节省轮胎。如果出现早期的红旗或安全车，他们希望能够换上一套全新的硬胎；而如果比赛后期发生撞车，他们则更倾向于额外进站换上全新的软胎或中性胎。
这正是法拉利的两位车手在第一节排位赛使用中性胎完成的原因，从而为正赛保留了一套全新的软胎。
倍耐力赛车运动主管达里奥·马拉福斯基对此表示：“我认为他们更放松了。在我看来，这是一个选择，是考虑到可能出现安全车（中文：中立化，英文：neutralisation）的情况。所以他们有一套全新的软胎，也许是为了比赛最后阶段在出现安全车时使用。
如果你按照一场正常比赛来起步，我们的建议是中性胎加硬胎，但如果在最后几圈出现安全车，他们手上还有一套全新的软胎。那将是一个巨大的优势，尽管无论如何超车都很困难。”
detailEn: What to expect from Madrid GP? From Mercedes' six-stop joke to a "six-kilometre-long" pitlane
Toto Wolff said that after FP1, Mercedes' strategy department was thinking about a six-stop race. In reality, the extremely long pitlane has drawn criticism and appears to favour a one-stopper

The circuit in Madrid has offered Formula 1 drivers a surprisingly high level of grip during their first visit, something that is certainly not a given at a new circuit. The grip level has taken some teams in the paddock by surprise, although the very high tyre degradation so far has done the same.

"It was tricky at the start of the weekend because this track has so much grip, even though it's a completely new asphalt surface," Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff said. "And interestingly enough, we have faced the exact opposite problem to what we expected.

"Based on how it looked after the first session, our strategy director said, ‘Six stops!’, because there was actually eight-tenths of degradation per lap. We've never seen that before, but in the end, I think it'll end up being a one-stop."
Why is tyre degradation so high in Madrid?

After Friday's practice sessions, tyre supplier Pirelli also expressed its surprise, not so much at the grip level – as that had already proved high during the pre-race measurements on Wednesday – but at the tyre degradation.

"Yes, honestly it has been a surprise," Pirelli chief engineer Simone Berra said when asked about it by Motorsport.com. "The teams are working on their set-ups to find the best compromise between the performance and long-run degradation. But, for sure, it's a surprise to have these kinds of values. They are outside our range of expectations."

Those values are not quite as extreme as Wolff suggested, but they are still noteworthy by F1 standards – something that is normally more characteristic of Qatar, a track where the heat is combined with a succession of high-speed corners. According to Pirelli, Friday saw two to three tenths of a second of lap time lost per lap purely through tyre degradation.
The Madring has offered a surprisingly good level of grip so far, but it’s very hard on the tyres
According to the Italian tyre supplier, the high degradation in Madrid has two underlying causes: graining and the usual thermal degradation at the rear axle.
"With this smooth tarmac and the high grip levels, we have graining generation," said Berra. "We basically reach the peak of the stress, so the tyre starts to tear and propagate graining.

"The graining level is for sure a limitation here, drivers can feel that there is a drop in performance. This is one of the effects that they have encountered during the high fuel runs on Friday, where front left graining was a limitation, inducing mid-corner understeer throughout the run. But we also had some thermal decay on the rear axle, so the combination of the two effects is generating a significant level of degradation."
F1 drivers criticise Madrid’s long pitlane

It will obviously not lead to six pitstops, but according to Pirelli it does make the strategic trade-off difficult. This is compounded by the fact that teams do not have a particularly large amount of long-run data following Arvid Lindblad's crash in FP2.
"What to expect for the race is already a question mark. I don't want to exclude any kind of situation," Berra said.
After the second practice session, Pirelli predicted a two-stopper, but a day later that prediction has been revised to a one-stopper. The reason is simple: the extremely long pitlane in Madrid.
Both Norris and Verstappen believe that the pitlane is far too long and highlights a design flaw

The pitlane is effectively split into two sections because part of the IFEMA complex sits in between. Although the pitlane does cut out Turns 1 and 2, drivers nevertheless believe it has been a major mistake in the Madring's design process.

"The pitlane is like six kilometres long!" said Lando Norris in the post-qualifying press conference. "We should have two parts of the pitlane: pit limiter, off pit limiter, and then pit limiter again. It’s the longest pit lane of the year and biggest pit loss of the year as well. That just makes overtaking worse.

"It makes the desire to box and do different strategies worse. If we’re going to build a new track and spend so much money on building a new track, this is probably one of the main factors, I would say, in making a track, to have a short pitlane so people can pit and then you create overtaking."

The long pitlane favours a one-stopper, despite the fact that according to Pirelli the pure race time is the same for one and two pitstops. Normally, that is a perfect scenario for creating strategic variation – which is exactly what Pirelli wants to achieve – but the Madrid pitlane could potentially ruin that.

An undercut relatively near the front of the field could trigger a second round of pitstops, but that is also a gamble, as track position is crucial in Madrid. Giving up track position for fresh rubber is risky, as Berra also acknowledges.

"The other factor is that, speaking with the teams, it seems quite difficult to overtake here," he said. "If you are in traffic, you lose quite a lot of performance and you destroy your tyres as well, because you lose load and generate higher temperatures. So the traffic can have a detrimental effect and is pushing towards the one-stop."
Apart from all the rational factors, misfortune in Madrid is just around the corner, as Bearman discovered on Saturday

Aside from these factors, a crash – and with it a safety car or red flag – also appears to be a distinct possibility in Madrid, meaning Lady Luck could play an even bigger role than any of the factors teams can rationally account for.

Teams need to be prepared for different scenarios, which is why some outfits have deliberately saved tyres on Friday and Saturday. In the event of an early red flag or safety car, they want to be able to switch to a new set of hard tyres, while in the event of a late crash they would prefer to make an additional pitstop for new softs or mediums.
That is precisely why the Ferrari drivers completed Q1 on mediums, leaving them with a set of fresh softs for the race.

"I think they are more relaxed," Pirelli’s head of motorsport Dario Marrafuschi said about that. "That was a choice, in my opinion, thinking of possible neutralisations. So they have a new set of soft, maybe for the last stint in case of a neutralisation.

"If you start a normal race, our suggestion is medium-hard, but in case of a neutralisation in the last laps, they have a new set of softs. That will be a great advantage, even though overtaking is difficult anyway."

items.summaryEn: Former McLaren F1 junior Ugo Ugochukwu was crowned the 2026 Formula 3 champion on Sunday, defeating Audi protege Freddie Slater. The pair had previously fought for the Formula Regional European title over the winter, with Ugochukwu prevailing there as well.
detailZh: 前迈凯伦F1青训车手Ugo Ugochukwu夺得F3年度冠军
Ugochukwu击败奥迪培养的Slater成为冠军
Ugo Ugochukwu于周日成为2026年F3年度冠军，尽管他在进入马德里赛道周末时还只是黑马。
整个夏季，Campos 比赛的Ugochukwu与Trident的Freddie Slater凭借在正赛中的稳定表现成为两位冠军争夺者。赛季前七轮（截至夏休期），Slater有六场正赛登上领奖台，Ugochukwu则有五场；没有其他车手在周日取得超过两次前三名。
作为奥迪新设立的车手发展项目的领军人物，Slater本有不错的机会在随后的Monza站对低调的Ugochukwu取得近乎决定性的优势。然而，他在冲刺赛获得第二名后，在正赛中从杆位逐渐掉队，并因技术故障退赛。
因此，这位18岁的英国车手带着仅15分的优势进入在马德里赛道举行的最后一站，领先19岁的美国车手。该站罕见地安排了三场比赛，以弥补因伊朗战争取消的巴林站。
然而Slater排位赛仅列第17和第8，这成为他的败因，而Ugochukwu在两节排位赛中分别排在第4和第2。
Freddie Slater在周日正赛中领先Yevan David
Ugochukwu在冲刺赛获得第八，在第一场正赛获得第四，而Slater未能得分，这意味着周日得分最多者将赢得冠军。
这位Campos车手跑了一场稳健的比赛，全程位居第二，既没有真正获得与Tuukka Taponen争夺胜利的机会，也无需防守自己的位置。
与此同时，他的Trident对手起步时被Yevan David超越，但在第五圈于1号弯外侧超过这位斯里兰卡车手，夺回第八位。但这远不足以击败Ugochukwu夺冠。
“感觉这场比赛比平时长得多，”这位美国人说。“由于乱流，要超越Tuukka相当困难。我努力了几圈，但我发现自己无法足够接近。我们知道第二名就能锁定冠军，所以最终只需把车带回。”
“每一处路肩听起来都比平时更响，我开始听到奇怪的声音，但我只能保持干净直到最后。一旦冲过终点线，我就可以放松了。真的如释重负。”
Ugo Ugochukwu停下赛车，成为F3新科冠军
有趣的是，两人此前曾在冬季争夺Formula Regional European年度冠军，Ugochukwu同样胜出。
这次成功对Ugochukwu而言如同救赎，他在去年年底离开迈凯伦青训项目，当时他的首个F3赛季仅列第16。
“我真的不知道该怎么感受，”他说。“感觉真的很好。我们整个赛季付出的努力终于得到了回报。这是一个了不起的赛季，我只想感谢我的车队Campos。我们全年合作得非常好，以这样的方式收尾是最好的结局。昨天锁定车队冠军，现在又拿下年度车手冠军，这几乎是一个完美的赛季。”
“这非常特别。我们在年初设定了目标，今天我们实现了它们。这非常好，”他补充道。
“我认为这个周末是最重要的一站。我们非常精准，整个周末没有犯错，我们在需要的时候拿出了表现并拿到了积分。这是结束赛季的完美方式。”
Slater仍获得本赛季F3最佳新秀的赞誉。
detailEn: Former McLaren F1 junior Ugo Ugochukwu wins Formula 3 title
Ugochukwu defeated Audi protege Slater to become champion
Ugo Ugochukwu became the 2026 Formula 3 champion on Sunday, despite coming into the Madring weekend as a dark horse.

Campos Racing’s Ugochukwu and Trident’s Freddie Slater emerged as the two title contenders over the summer, courtesy of their consistency in feature races. In the first seven rounds of the season – until the summer break – Slater finished six feature races on the podium, while Ugochukwu stood at five; no other drivers took more than two top-three finishes on Sunday.

Spearheading Audi’s new Driver Development Programme, Slater had a decent chance of taking a near-decisive edge over a low-key Ugochukwu in the following Monza round. However, after finishing second in the sprint, he gradually dropped down the order from pole position in the feature race and retired due to a technical issue.

The 18-year-old Briton therefore went into the final round, at Madring, with just a 15-point advantage over the 19-year-old American. The round unusually featured three races to make up for the loss of the Bahrain event due to the Iran war.
Slater however qualified down in 17th and eighth, which proved to be his downfall, while Ugochukwu was fourth and second across the two qualifying sessions.
Freddie Slater leading Yevan David in Sunday's feature race
Ugochukwu finished eighth in the sprint and fourth in the first feature race while Slater failed to score, meaning whoever scored the most points on Sunday would win the title.
The Campos driver had a solid race, which he spent in second place without really getting a chance to fight Tuukka Taponen for the win or having to defend his position.

Meanwhile, his Trident counterpart lost a spot to Yevan David at the start, but passed the Sri Lankan around the outside of Turn 1 on lap five to retrieve eighth position. This was far from enough though to beat Ugochukwu to the crown.

“It felt like a much longer race than usual,” the American said. “It was quite difficult with the dirty air to overtake Tuukka. I tried my best a few laps, but I saw I couldn’t get quite close enough. We knew that P2 would clinch the title, so just had to ultimately bring it home.
“Every single kerb felt louder than usual, I started hearing weird sounds, but I just had to keep it clean until the end. Once I crossed the finish line, I could relax. Just really relieved.”
Ugo Ugochukwu comes to a halt as F3's new champion
Interestingly, the pair previously fought for the Formula Regional European title over the winter, with Ugochukwu prevailing too.
This success will taste like redemption to Ugochukwu, who left the McLaren junior programme at the end of last year after finishing his maiden F3 season down in 16th.

“I don’t really know what to feel,” he said. “It feels really good. The work we put in throughout the entire season finally paid off. It’s been an amazing campaign, and I just want to thank my team, Campos. We worked really well together all year, and to finish off like this is the best possible way. Clinching the teams’ championship yesterday and now the drivers’ one as well is pretty much a perfect season."
“[It’s] super special. We had our goals set out at the beginning of the year, and today we have achieved them. It’s been super good," he added.

“I think this weekend was the one which really mattered the most. We were super clinical, no mistakes made the whole weekend, and we just delivered when we had to and picked up the points. Perfect way to end the season.”
Slater still takes plaudits as F3’s top rookie this season.
